name: Credit rating agencies
payer: Issuer pays since the 1970s; investor-pays subscription model before that.
access: Non-public issuer information under confidentiality (Regulation FD exemption).
publication: Ratings public; methodologies disclosed by regulation after 2010.
ai_analogue: A payer-conflicted assurance market that regulators chose to license and supervise rather than restructure. Outcomes in 2008 show the limits of disclosure and licensing without liability or competition.

milestones.event: Moody's publishes the first bond ratings, sold to investors by subscription.
Penn Central default; agencies begin charging issuers rather than investors.
Issuer-pays model makes the rated party the client.
SEC creates the NRSRO designation, embedding ratings in regulation.
Credit Rating Agency Reform Act formalizes NRSRO registration and SEC oversight.
Structured-finance ratings fail in the financial crisis.
Dodd-Frank Title IX: SEC Office of Credit Ratings, methodology disclosure, analyst separation from sales, expanded liability exposure.

status: seed; secondary sources; verify each milestone against a primary source before citing in the paper
